notes:
Executive summary: Pinnacle (global payments consortium) evaluating Redwood Dedicated for transaction enrichment, chat assistant, and real-time fraud reranking. Primary asks: contractual SLA with uptime >= 99.995% for critical endpoints, credits tied to 15-minute P1 windows; 24/7 premium support with 60-min P1 response and 4-hr P2 response.

POC highlights:
- Provisioned equivalent of 32 GPUs (8x V100-equivalent groups) sustained peak throughput: ~60k tokens/min aggregated.
- Latency: p50 28ms (short chat prompts), p95 90ms for single-turn chat, p95 150ms for 2k-token model runs during POC burst tests.
- KV/prefix caching reduced token compute by ~22% on repeat flows; batching configuration tuned for 8-12ms per-token overhead.

SLA / Contract priorities called out by customer:
- Uptime: target 99.995% for "critical" inference routes used during settlement windows.
- Credits: want explicit credit schedule per 15-minute windows (not daily aggregated). Suggests higher weight for peak hours.
- Maintenance: only 1x weekly maintenance window allowed and must be Sunday 02:00-06:00 UTC for production; no maintenance on weekdays 08:00-18:00 PST. Advance notice minimum 21 days for major upgrades.
- Support: defined escalation matrix, named engineers for P0/P1, runbook hand-off for on-call.
- Reserved capacity mapping: request clear translation table ("X reserved GPUs maps to Y sustained qps at avg 2k tokens") and fallback model variants with throughput guarantees.
- Legal redlines: limit force majeure carve-outs, clarity on indemnity related to model outputs, strict EU data residency and proof of controls for EU cardholder data.

Quote from CTO on 2026-02-18 call: "We need deterministic throughput guarantees — can't have noisy neighbor degradation during peak settlement windows. If you can map reserved capacity to billing/credits precisely, multi-year commit is likely."

Commercial posture: mid-high cost sensitivity; willing to sign 2-3 year commit if SLA and GPU-to-throughput mapping explicit. Interested in long-term discount tiers and dedicated hardware placement (pinned racks) for top-of-stack performance.

Open questions for Redwood to answer before exec sign-off:
- Provide formal SLA draft with credit matrix and examples (15-min sliding window).
- Deliver GPU-to-throughput mapping table for 1k/2k/5k token averages.
- Confirm maintenance blackout enforcement and notification process.
- Provide updated security FAQ showing evidence of SOC2 + EU data residency handling.

Next actions (short): Redwood to deliver redlined SLA by 2026-03-15; SE (Nora) to provide detailed throughput mapping and updated POC perf artifacts. Legal to exchange redlines. Exec demo scheduled week of 2026-03-22.
